summary.en: Bandits have intensified attacks in Niger, killing village heads, beheading leaders, burning houses and a palace, and abducting residents in villages such as Lumma Ba’are and Borgu. The Burkina Faso junta is accused of targeting journalists, activists and opposition exiles abroad. Human Rights Watch reports these repressive actions against media and civil society. The conflict continues to generate high mortality, with 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. Recent incidents show a surge in bandit violence and state repression alongside the ongoing jihadist threat in the Sahel.

background.title: War in the Sahel
background.extract: The War in the Sahel, also known as the Sahel War, is a multi-sided armed conflict that has been ongoing since 2012. The conflict mainly takes place in the countries of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso.
